short_title: Quantitative evaluation of fracture porosity from dual laterolog based on deep learning
formation: Not named beyond 'carbonate rocks', Tahe oilfield S block (Ordovician carbonate play)
depth_range: Not explicitly reported (well examples S-4, S-7)
no_wells: 2 real wells (S-4, S-7) used ONLY for qualitative benchmark; 0 real wells in training (100% synthetic training)
target_property: Fracture porosity (FP, continuous) + fracture dip angle (FDA, 0-90 deg)
target_units_definition: FP in %, from equivalent macroscopic anisotropic fracture model; FDA in degrees, binned into low(0-50), medium(50-74), high(74-90) angle categories
reference_label_source: SYNTHETIC ONLY - 3D finite-element (3DFE) forward-modeled dual-laterolog (DLL) responses from a parallel-fracture equivalent-anisotropic model. Real wells (S-4,S-7) used only as a qualitative benchmark vs FMI-derived fracture porosity (P33), not as ML train/test labels.
predictor_logs: Dual laterolog only: deep laterolog resistivity (Rlld), shallow laterolog resistivity (Rlls)
feature_engineering: Physics-based synthetic feature space: bedrock resistivity (Rb), fracture-fluid resistivity (Rf), fracture dip angle (Omega), fracture thickness (h), fracture spacing (d) -> forward-modeled via 3DFE to produce >500,000 synthetic (input->DLL response) pairs; DNN (5-input, 256-neuron hidden layers, ReLU) trained as a fast surrogate for the slow 3DFE forward model; inversion via Newton-Cotes/gradient-descent with multi-initial-value strategy; resistivity binned into 8 ranges, dip angle discretized every 0.5 deg
ml_algorithms: Deep Neural Network (DNN) used as a forward-model surrogate (not a direct field-log classifier/regressor) + gradient-descent/Newton-Cotes inversion algorithm
validation_strategy_described: Synthetic self-consistency verification only: DNN forward-model outputs vs 3DFE ground truth; inversion recovery of known synthetic FP/FDA values. Real-well application (S-4, S-7) validated only qualitatively/visually against FMI-derived P33 and an older method (SFCM) - no independent quantitative real-well validation.
validation_level_raw_extraction: Not applicable / Level 0 (numerical self-consistency on synthetic data); no field-level validation level achieved (qualitative-only for real wells)
performance_train: Synthetic DNN-vs-3DFE MAE: 3.15e-5 to 2.47e-5 Ohm.m (resistivity, angle-dependent, self-consistency); FP inversion MAE 0.00166-0.0035% (Rb>1000 Ohm.m) and 0.003-0.019% (100-1000 Ohm.m); dip-angle misclassification at bin boundaries up to ~36%
performance_test_val: Real wells S-4, S-7: qualitative visual match only to FMI-derived P33 and SFCM method; no R2/RMSE/MAE reported for real-well predictions
sample_size_train: >500,000 synthetic 3DFE-generated samples (DNN training); ~1900-2088 synthetic verification sets across 3 dip-angle categories
sample_size_test: 2 real wells (S-4, S-7), qualitative comparison only - no quantified real test set
leakage_independence_notes: N/A in the conventional sense (100% synthetic training data, no real-sample leakage possible). Key methodological caveat instead: the quantitative accuracy figures reported are self-consistency checks of the DNN against the SAME 3DFE physics model used to generate its own training data - a form of circularity if read as generalization evidence. The only real-world check is qualitative/visual on 2 wells.
notes_caveats: METHODOLOGICALLY DISTINCT from nearly all other papers in this review: this is a physics-informed / synthetic-training DNN-surrogate + inversion approach, not ML trained directly on real labeled field data. Needs explicit discussion as its own category in the manuscript's ML taxonomy (Section 4/5) - conflating its low synthetic MAE with real predictive accuracy would overstate the evidence. Recommend citing as an example of the 'prediction vs explanation / synthetic self-consistency vs real generalization' distinction central to the review's critical framework.

short_title: Identification of natural fractures using fracture signature function and ML
basin_field: Sichuan Basin, Changning-Zhutong area (southern Sichuan), China
lithology: Organic-rich shale with interbedded carbonate-rich layers; clayey/bioclastic lithofacies variation with depth
reservoir_type: Shale gas, naturally fractured (microfractures + natural open fractures)
no_wells: Not explicitly itemized as a well count; single reservoir interval analyzed with N=1907 total logged samples
target_units_definition: NF class picked from FMI (formation image log)
reference_label_source: FMI (formation micro-imager) fracture picks; 28 fractures identified with true dip ~50-65 deg, true dip azimuth 100-175 deg
predictor_logs: 8 conventional logs: GR, Cal (caliper), DEN (density), DTC (compressional sonic), DTS (shear sonic), RXO (shallow resistivity), RT (deep resistivity), CNL (neutron)
feature_engineering: Novel 'Fracture Signature Function' (FSFn'') equation: 5 log-specific base equations (gamma ray A, resistivity B, caliper C, sonic D, density E; Table 1) normalized per 8 GR-defined lithological zones, linearly combined (FSF=An+Bn+Cn+Dn+En), then differentiated via a finite-difference derivative (Q(h)) to produce FSFn' and a second derivative FSFn''; SMOTE and Random Oversampling (ROS) applied for class-imbalance correction on ML models (not on the FSFn equation itself, which needs no training)
ml_algorithms: XGBoost, Decision Tree, Random Forest, SVM, Feed-Forward Neural Network (FNN, 3 layers 128-64-32), Recurrent Neural Network (RNN, 128 neurons/2 layers) - each combined with SMOTE and ROS variants; plus the standalone (non-ML) FSFn'' equation
validation_strategy_described: Random 70/30 train-test split (Level 1); no blind-well or depth-block holdout
validation_level_raw_extraction: Level 1 (random sample split)
performance_train: Not separately itemized (only test-set/confusion-matrix metrics given)
performance_test_val: Accuracy/Precision/Recall/Specificity/F1 (%): XGBoost_SMOTE 84.7/9.4/18.5/88.8/12.5; XGBoost_ROS 91.7/0/0/97.4/0; DT_SMOTE 84.7/7.8/14.8/89.1/10.2; DT_ROS 91.2/15.7/11.1/96.2/13.0; RF_SMOTE 93.8/17.2/18.5/94.4/17.8; RF_ROS 89.9/0/0/99.7/0; SVM_SMOTE 67/11.8/81.4/61.6/21.1; SVM_ROS 61.7/11.4/81.4/60.5/20.2; FNN 79.2/-/40.2/-/18.8 (recall); RNN 82.1/-/-/-/6.8. AUC: RF(SMOTE)=0.80, XGBoost(SMOTE)=0.76, SVM(SMOTE)=0.72, DT(ROS)=0.54; FNN AUC=0.88, RNN AUC=0.83. FSFn'' equation: qualitative match to FMI-picked fractures, with noted failures in narrow/borehole-affected zones (e.g. near 2425 m, caliper-affected).
leakage_independence_notes: Random sample-level (Level-1) split only - no well/depth-block holdout; severe class imbalance (minority fracture class ~5% of N=1907, confirmed by NF descriptive stats mean=0.05) drives the accuracy/F1 divergence.
notes_caveats: One of the strongest illustrative cases in the whole batch for the review's core critique 'High R2/accuracy != Reliable Subsurface Transferability': RF's 91% accuracy but 17.6% F1 is a textbook class-imbalance failure mode. The authors' own proposed FSFn'' equation (non-ML, physically-motivated) is offered as an alternative precisely because the ML models proved unreliable under class imbalance - useful contrast between engineered-equation and trained-model approaches for the review's Section 5.
